title: Neural Topic Modeling via Contextual and Graph Information Fusion
subcategory: VAE-based NTM with contextual (BERT) and word co-occurrence graph fusion
task: Topic discovery with interpretable topic-word and document-topic distributions
problem: Existing NTMs produce uninformative or incoherent topics; contextual (PLM) information is used in isolation or not combined well with TF-IDF/BoW information.
architecture: CGTM: VAE framework with a Siamese encoder that yields a BoW/TF-IDF topic proportion and a BERT-based contextual topic proportion, fused with a Dirichlet-drawn weight; topic alignment and topic sharpening constraints; a BoW decoder plus a GraphDecoder that reconstructs a corpus-level word co-occurrence graph (graph information fusion).
llm_or_encoder: BERT representations; LLM used only for label-alignment evaluation

datasets.name: 20News
datasets.details: 11,314 train / 7,531 test, vocab 3,997, avg length 64.8, 20 labels

datasets.name: NYT
datasets.details: 7,456 train / 5,233 test, vocab 8,174, avg length 272.2, 29 labels

datasets.name: AGnews
datasets.details: 59,000 train / 3,800 test, vocab 4,422, avg length 19.1, 4 labels (short text)

key_results: Best NPMI on the three datasets; the strongest graph baseline (GINopic) obtains NPMI about 20% lower.
Human evaluation: WIS 0.750 vs 0.530 for GINopic (best baseline), a 31% gain; TIS 0.713, tied with GINopic.
strengths: Combines TF-IDF and BERT information at the topic level rather than by simple concatenation.
Uses both automatic and human evaluation, plus LLM-based label alignment.

limitations.text: Directly enhancing topic interpretability remains hard; the authors suggest LLM-based approaches such as TopicGPT as future work.
Topic intrusion does not account for topic repetition and may inflate scores; it also needs time-consuming manual evaluation.
Time complexity could be reduced further.

notes: Statistical significance reported (p < 0.05) for improvements over best baseline.
